claim.markdown_says: ### **A.1 Implementor-defined language element list**   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 38880; compare line 39466 '## A.2 Undefined language element list', line 39672 '## A.3 Processor-dependent language element list', line 39846 '## A.4 Optional language element list')
claim.why_it_matters: A.1 is emitted at h3 with an extra bold wrapper while its siblings A.2, A.3 and A.4 are emitted at h2 unadorned. The outline shows A.1 nested one level below A.2-A.4 instead of alongside them, and the bold markers become part of the heading text, so an exact heading-text match on 'A.1 Implementor-defined language element list' fails.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on three independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The rendered PDF page 973 (printed folio 943) prints the bold heading 'A.1 Implementor-defined language element list'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 38880 carries that heading with every word present, in order, verbatim. The only textual difference is that the PDF's wide tab gap between 'A.1' and 'Implementor-defined' is transcribed as a single space -- exactly as it is for A.2, A.3 and A.4, whose PDF headings use the identical tab. Kind 'missing-heading' is therefore inapplicable: the heading is present and its meaning is unchanged. (2) THE DIAGNOSIS IS INVERTED -- A.1 IS THE CONFORMANT HEADING, NOT THE DEVIANT ONE. The transcription's document-wide annex convention is h2 for the annex title and h3 for its numbered subsections. Verified across the whole file: '## Annex B' -> '### B.1 General' / '### B.2 Notation' / '### B.3 Repertoire of characters permitted in user-defined words'; '## Annex C' -> '### C.1 Notations'; '### D.1 General'; '### E.1 General'; '### F.1 Archaic language elements'. Annex A itself follows it internally at '### A.4.1 General', '### A.4.2 ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling', '### A.4.12 RESUME statement', '### A.4.13 REWRITE FILE and WRITE FILE', '### A.4.14 VALIDATE'. A.1 at h3 under '## Annex A' matches that convention. It is A.2 (39466), A.3 (39672) and A.4 (39846) that are wrongly promoted to h2, which makes them siblings of '## Annex A' rather than its children. The claim asks to demote A.1 to match three outliers, which would move the file further from its own convention. (3) THE 'EXACT HEADING-TEXT MATCH FAILS' RATIONALE IS FALSE. '**...**' inside an ATX heading is inline emphasis; a markdown parser yields the heading's text content as exactly 'A.1 Implementor-defined language element list'. Only a naive raw-line string compare sees the asterisks, and that is a defect in the matcher, not in the transcription. The bold is also faithful to the PDF, where the heading is genuinely set in bold. PDF TYPOGRAPHY, READ DIRECTLY. I rendered both pages at 300 dpi and compared the printed glyphs. Page 973 sets 'A.1 Implementor-defined language element list' in bold serif at the left margin. Page 993 (folio 963) sets 'A.2 Undefined language element list' in bold serif at the same left margin, same cap height, same weight, same number-tab-title pattern. The two headings are typographically IDENTICAL in the PDF, and page 993 carries no annex title above A.2 -- confirming the PDF treats A.1 and A.2 as peer subsections of Annex A. The PDF therefore encodes no level distinction at all between them, so it cannot be the source of a level discrepancy. NET: the difference between the two sources here is confined to markdown heading-level and emphasis markup. No word of the specification text differs and no meaning changes, which falls squarely under the 'formatting only' rejection criterion. USEFUL RESIDUE (markdown-internal, not a PDF discrepancy): the transcription is genuinely self-inconsistent in Annex A, and A.1 also lacks a '' anchor while section-a-2, section-a-3, section-a-4, section-b-1, section-b-2 and section-c-1 all have one. If anyone chooses to tidy this, the correct repair is to demote A.2/A.3/A.4 to h3 and add the missing section-a-1 anchor -- the opposite of what this claim proposes. Anchors are transcription scaffolding absent from the PDF, so this remains outside the PDF-vs-markdown ledger.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. The heading 'A.1 Implementor-defined language element list' is present verbatim at line 38880 and matches the PDF word for word; only markdown heading-level and bold markup differ, and the PDF encodes no level distinction whatsoever (A.1 on page 973 and A.2 on page 993 are typeset identically in bold at the same margin). The claim is additionally inverted: A.1's h3 is correct per the transcription's document-wide annex convention ('## Annex X' -> '### X.n', as at B.1, B.2, B.3, C.1, D.1, E.1, F.1 and A.4.1/A.4.2/A.4.12-A.4.14); the real outliers are A.2, A.3 and A.4 at h2. The 'exact heading-text match fails' rationale is also wrong -- '**' inside an ATX heading is inline emphasis, so a markdown parser reports the heading text as exactly 'A.1 Implementor-defined language element list'.
